# requireArray

<link-summary>Returns the value as an array, or throws.</link-summary>

<web-summary>requireArray() — Returns the value as an array, or throws. apps-script-utils, English.</web-summary>

<tldr>
<p>Module: <code>lang/base</code> · Since: 1.11.0</p>
</tldr>

```typescript
function requireArray<T>(value: unknown, message: string = "Expected an array."): T[];
```

`Array.isArray` is the whole test, so an array from another frame counts and an array-like object — `arguments`, a `NodeList`, `{ length: 0 }` — does not.

`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).

## Parameters

| Parameter                                       | Type      | Description                                                   |
| :---------------------------------------------- | :-------- | :------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `value`                                         | `unknown` | The value to validate.                                        |
| `message` _(optional)_ `= "Expected an array."` | `string`  | The message of the exception. A default is used when omitted. |

## Returns

`T[]` — the same value, typed as an array.

## Throws

| Exception                  | Condition                  |
| :------------------------- | :------------------------- |
| `IllegalArgumentException` | the value is not an array. |

## Examples

### What passes and what does not

```javascript
requireArray([]); // => []
requireArray([1, 2, 3]); // => [1, 2, 3]
requireArray("abc"); // throws IllegalArgumentException
requireArray({ length: 0 }); // throws IllegalArgumentException
```
